questions.question: What source-labelled trip or interlock records apply to each rotating or fired machine, and what remains unverified?

evidence.text: equipment K-201 reads "K-201 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, low stage (booster)"
equipment K-202 reads "K-202 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage"
equipment K-203 reads "K-203 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage (trim)"
equipment AC-501 reads "AC-501 Instrument air compressor"

data_requests.item: Cause-and-effect matrix and HAZOP/LOPA records
where: site records: cause-and-effect matrix, HAZOP and LOPA reports
DCS/PLC configuration: safety system configuration
data_requests.how: Review existing cause-and-effect, governing requirements and configuration records for each named machine, with their revisions and applicability. Retain supplied trip/switch indications as candidates; a drawing label or an unrelated function does not settle the records or establish effective, tested protection. Missing model information is not evidence that installed protection is absent.

data_requests.item: Machine/function association and current evidence
where: site records: source-labelled function identifiers, initiating measurements, final elements and protected-machine targets, shared scope and revisions; governing requirements and validation/test evidence where applicable
DCS/PLC configuration: existing configuration and its documented measurement/action/final-element identities, read through the approved site process
data_requests.how: Keep each machine in the review even where a switch or trip is supplied. Retain all explicit shared targets and supplied qualifiers; unknown or contradictory targets remain unresolved. Same-model text or nearby equipment does not prove function coverage. Record a responsible person or authority separately from protected-machine association; neither is inferred here. This requests record review, not a new test, safety design or operating action.

questions.decision_rule: A qualified site review may resolve the source-labelled machine/function associations and remaining record requests using applicable current evidence. A supplied trip, switch, cause/effect row or shared-function label alone establishes neither complete coverage nor installed protection adequacy. This screen grants no acceptance or authority and performs no safety validation.

typical_benefit.wording: Safety benefit; no energy source. Present it as a question to verify, not a finding.

questions.limits: P&IDs often leave trips to separate cause-and-effect records. Missing or unknown model evidence does not establish missing installed protection. Supplied associations, shared targets, revisions and contradictions require review; no machine, person owner, approval, tested condition or effective protection is inferred. C9 has no primary safety-design source cited in the catalog and remains a question for record review, not safety design, SIL assignment, a legal-compliance assessment or an operating recommendation.

questions.question: Is this refrigeration condenser train's head pressure appropriate for its weather, operating limits and actual reset coverage?

evidence.text: equipment C-201 reads "C-201 Ammonia evaporative condenser"
instrument PT-203 reads "PT-203 Condenser head (discharge) pressure" at C-201
controller PIC-203 reads "PIC-203 Head pressure control at a fixed setpoint, on the condenser fans" at C-201
equipment K-201 reads "K-201 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, low stage (booster)"
equipment K-202 reads "K-202 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage"
equipment K-203 reads "K-203 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage (trim)"
instrument JT-201 reads "JT-201 Low-stage compressor motor power" at K-201

data_requests.item: Head (discharge) pressure and condensing temperature, hourly over a year
where: historian or DCS trend for PT-203 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: the head pressure setpoint and its low limit in the refrigeration plant controls
data_requests.how: Convert pressure to saturated condensing temperature with the refrigerant's tables; see whether it falls in cool weather or sits at the setpoint.

data_requests.item: Ambient wet-bulb temperature (dry-bulb for an air-cooled condenser) at the same times
where: site records: the site weather station, or the nearest public weather station's hourly record
data_requests.how: Line it up hour by hour with the condensing temperature.

data_requests.item: The lowest head pressure the plant can run at
where: DCS/PLC configuration: the minimum needed for hot gas defrost, liquid injection oil cooling and liquid feed to the farthest evaporator
the vendor datasheet: compressor and expansion valve minimum pressure difference
data_requests.how: This is the floor a floating setpoint may not go below.

data_requests.item: Compressor and condenser fan and pump power
where: historian or DCS trend for JT-201 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
a walkdown: power logger on the compressor motors and on the condenser fan and spray pump motors
data_requests.how: Floating the head pressure moves load from the compressors to the condenser fans; count both.

data_requests.item: Condenser-train coverage and applicable head-pressure operating basis
where: site records: source-labelled compressor discharge/header, condenser, sensor, controller, fan/pump and served-demand membership; actual reset scope, enabled/as-operated mode, revision and unknown or contradictory targets for this train

DCS/PLC configuration: existing representative coincident head-pressure/condensing-temperature, ambient and power records; stated minimum-pressure constraints and applicable periods before further collection through the approved site process
data_requests.how: Keep this condenser train in the review even when local, shared, unrelated, negated or disabled reset text is supplied. Such records are candidates, not proof of current mode, complete coverage or suitable data. Verify exact train membership, pressure units/reference, refrigerant and saturation basis, appropriate wet-bulb or dry-bulb weather/sensor basis, coincident periods and relevant defrost, oil-cooling, feed and vendor constraints. Retain raw targets, revisions and qualifiers; unknown or contradictory scope stays unresolved. Compare total affected compressor and condenser fan/pump demand before drawing an economic conclusion. This requests existing records and qualified review, not a setpoint change, control design or operating action.

questions.decision_rule: Review only after source-qualified train membership, actual operating/reset mode, coincident representative observations, applicable pressure limits and total affected power are established. Fixed-head behavior may justify investigation, while an operating reset may narrow the question, but a supplied label or one scalar does not close coverage or suitability. No setpoint or operating change is inferred.

typical_benefit.wording: Floating head pressure (S25, p. 62) "allows compressor head pressures to move up or down with variations in ambient wet-bulb temperature, saving energy compared to fixed head pressure operation." Condensing pressure (S25, p. 65): "Lowering the condensing temperature can reduce compressor energy use by around 2% to 3% for every degree Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit) of temperature reduction (SenterNovem 2003)." Condenser fans (S25, p. 65): "On systems where floating head operation is stable, ASDs can lower condenser fan energy consumption by up to 40% compared to operating a fixed-speed condenser fan in on/off fashion (IRC 2004b)."
source_titles: S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: S25 (p. 62) warns that condenser fan energy rises as head pressure falls and that head pressure must not go below what defrost or liquid injection oil cooling need. Fires only where the equipment's own name, type or service names the refrigerant (ammonia, NH3, R-717, a refrigerant number) or says refrigeration; an air compressor, a process recycle compressor, a process condenser on cooling water or a power-plant air-cooled condenser does not. All shown measurements, compressors, power readings and reset labels remain source candidates; the screen does not infer condenser-train membership, actual mode, constraints or data suitability. Arbitrary source facts/qualifiers are not all rendered by the screen: retain its source record pointers and the original model, and inspect complete graph/context records for supported values. Even an explicitly shared reset does not discharge the applicable operating-basis request.

questions.question: Does each refrigeration suction level match the conditions required by every coincident load it serves?

evidence.text: equipment K-201 reads "K-201 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, low stage (booster)"
equipment K-202 reads "K-202 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage"
equipment K-203 reads "K-203 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage (trim)"
instrument PT-201 reads "PT-201 Low-stage suction pressure" at K-201
instrument PT-202 reads "PT-202 High-stage suction pressure" at K-202
equipment EV-201 reads "EV-201 Spiral freezer evaporator (ammonia, hot gas defrost)"
equipment EV-202 reads "EV-202 Frozen store unit cooler (ammonia, hot gas defrost)"
equipment CS-201 reads "CS-201 Frozen product cold store"
instrument TT-205 reads "TT-205 Spiral freezer air temperature" at EV-201
instrument TT-206 reads "TT-206 Frozen store air temperature" at EV-202
instrument JT-201 reads "JT-201 Low-stage compressor motor power" at K-201

data_requests.item: Suction pressure at each suction level, hourly
where: historian or DCS trend for PT-201, PT-202 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: suction pressure setpoints per compressor or suction level
data_requests.how: Retain refrigerant identity, pressure reference and measurement location before relating suction pressure to saturated evaporating temperature. Match the operating periods of pressures, setpoints and loads; distinguish stages and pressure drops. No setpoint is calculated here.

data_requests.item: The temperature each load actually needs
where: site records: room and product temperature specifications for each freezer, cold store and chiller, and which suction level serves it
historian or DCS trend for TT-205, TT-206 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
data_requests.how: For every coincident load, establish its required temperature and required heat-transfer approach, and the suction level actually serving it. The most demanding admissible evaporating condition across those loads constrains a shared level; the warmest load alone does not govern. This is an engineering constraint to review, not a quotation from the cited two-stage example or a plant setpoint recommendation.

data_requests.item: Compressor power and run hours per suction level
where: historian or DCS trend for JT-201 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
site records: compressor run hours from the refrigeration plant controls
data_requests.how: A month or more at normal production.

data_requests.item: Suction-level membership and reset coverage
where: site records: source-labelled compressor, suction header and served-load membership; reset strategy and coverage for each level, with stage and pressure-regulation boundaries
data_requests.how: Drawn reset indications are candidates only. Confirm ownership and shared-level coverage; a reset on another compressor does not settle these loads. Unknown connections, applicable approaches and product or quality constraints remain open for qualified review.

questions.decision_rule: Study a level only after mapping every coincident served load and reviewing its required temperature, approach and operating constraints against the actual level and reset coverage. A colder-than-required level may warrant investigation, but the most demanding admissible evaporating condition across all served loads constrains any change. A drawn reset, ambient change or warm load alone does not settle the question. The cited benefit remains a conditional two-stage low-stage example; no setpoint or savings is calculated.

typical_benefit.wording: Two-stage systems (S25, p. 63): "a simple way to save energy is to raise the suction pressure and temperature of the low-stage compressor when ambient temperatures decrease. It has been estimated that energy savings of about 8% can be realized in two-stage systems when suction temperatures are raised from -30 °F to -20 °F (ISU 2005)." No figure is given there for single-stage systems.
source_titles: S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: Product temperature and food-safety limits set the floor: a suction change changes how product is held and needs the quality owner's sign-off. Fires only where the equipment's own name, type or service names the refrigerant (ammonia, NH3, R-717, a refrigerant number) or says refrigeration; an air compressor, a process recycle compressor, a process condenser on cooling water or a power-plant air-cooled condenser does not. Drawn reset text does not prove usable operating observations or all-load coverage. Shared headers, different approaches, pressure regulation, stages, transients and equipment limits can change the governing condition; keep topology and applicability unverified until reviewed.

questions.question: Does this refrigeration compressor carry part load on its slide valve (or hot gas bypass) with no speed control?

evidence.text: equipment K-201 reads "K-201 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, low stage (booster)"
instrument JT-201 reads "JT-201 Low-stage compressor motor power" at K-201
no variable speed drive or speed controller drawn on this compressor

data_requests.item: Slide valve (capacity) position over normal operation
where: DCS/PLC configuration: slide valve position or percent capacity per compressor from the refrigeration plant controls, a month or more
data_requests.how: Hours spent below full load, by load band.

data_requests.item: Compressor power and run hours
where: historian or DCS trend for JT-201 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
a walkdown: power logger on the compressor motor across a normal week
data_requests.how: Power at each load band, so part-load efficiency can be seen.

data_requests.item: How the compressors are sequenced
where: DCS/PLC configuration: which compressor trims, and the order and pressures at which they load and unload
data_requests.how: Note whether more than one machine trims at the same time.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a look when screws spend long hours part-loaded on the slide valve while another could be off, or when no machine on a suction level has speed control to trim. Close it if each runs near full load or a sequencer already keeps one machine trimming.

typical_benefit.wording: Among control strategies that "may compromise system energy efficiency" (S25, p. 59, citing Pearson 2003): "Slide valve unloading of oversized screw compressors." and "Hot gas bypass of compressors." Speed control (S25, p. 63): "ASDs used on compressors below a part-load ratio of about 95% will deliver performance equal to a fixed speed compressor but with lower electricity requirements. However, at near full (i.e., 100%) load, ASDs are approximately 3% less efficient than fixed speed drives".
source_titles: S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: A drive or sequencing change goes through the compressor vendor (minimum speed, oil management, vibration). questions.question: Are these evaporators defrosted on a fixed timer rather than when frost is actually there?

evidence.text: equipment EV-201 reads "EV-201 Spiral freezer evaporator (ammonia, hot gas defrost)"
final element HGV-201 reads "HGV-201 Hot gas defrost valve, spiral freezer evaporator (defrost started by a timer)" at EV-201
instrument TT-205 reads "TT-205 Spiral freezer air temperature" at EV-201
no demand defrost initiation (coil differential pressure, frost sensor) drawn on this evaporator

data_requests.item: Defrost schedule per evaporator
where: DCS/PLC configuration: defrost initiation (timer or demand), defrosts per day, duration and termination (time or coil temperature) per evaporator
data_requests.how: List defrosts per day by season.

data_requests.item: Frost on the coil when a scheduled defrost starts
where: a walkdown: look at the coil just before a few scheduled defrosts, in a dry week and a humid week
data_requests.how: Note clear, light or heavy frost.

data_requests.item: Hot gas use and room temperature rise per defrost
where: historian or DCS trend for HGV-201 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
historian or DCS trend for TT-205 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
data_requests.how: The heat put in to defrost comes back as refrigeration load afterwards.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a look when coils are clear at scheduled defrosts, or the count per day is the same in dry weeks as in humid ones. Close it if defrost is already started on demand.

typical_benefit.wording: Demand defrost (S25, p. 66): "Evaporators should be defrosted only when necessary, as opposed to on timed schedules where defrosting occurs regardless of need." "Too frequent defrosts." is listed among control strategies that "may compromise system energy efficiency" (S25, p. 59, citing Pearson 2003). No % stated.
source_titles: S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: A coil differential pressure instrument on the evaporator is taken as demand defrost; check that it is used for that. A P&ID rarely shows the defrost timer itself, so the schedule always comes from the controls.

questions.question: Does this oven, dryer or fryer send its hot exhaust to atmosphere with no heat recovery on it?

evidence.text: equipment D-301 reads "D-301 Gas-fired product dryer (continuous belt)"
stream S1 (asset stream:S1) reads "Dryer exhaust air to atmosphere"
instrument TT-304 reads "TT-304 Dryer exhaust air temperature" at D-301
stream U1 (asset stream:U1) reads "Natural gas to the dryer burner" at D-301
instrument FT-301 reads "FT-301 Dryer burner natural gas flow" at D-301
valve TV-301 reads "TV-301 Dryer burner natural gas control valve" at D-301
no heat recovery exchanger, recuperator, run-around coil or exhaust recirculation on this unit or on a stream drawn from it

data_requests.item: Exhaust temperature and flow
where: historian or DCS trend for TT-304 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
a walkdown: thermometer and a pitot or anemometer traverse in the exhaust duct, at normal production
data_requests.how: Record both at normal production; heat on offer = mass flow x specific heat x (exhaust temperature minus the temperature it could be cooled to).

data_requests.item: Exhaust moisture and contaminants
where: a walkdown: humidity or dew point probe in the exhaust; note fat, flour, sugar or product dust
maintenance records: duct and stack cleaning history
data_requests.how: Moist exhaust carries latent heat but condenses; fat and dust foul exchangers unless filtered or washed.

data_requests.item: Fuel or heat input and operating hours
where: historian or DCS trend for FT-301 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
utility bills or the site energy report: gas sub-meter readings for this line
site records: production schedule: hours per week the line runs
data_requests.how: A month of input at a known production rate.

data_requests.item: Where the heat could go in the unit itself
where: site records: inlet (drying or combustion) air temperature and flow
a walkdown: room next to the unit for ductwork or a run-around coil
data_requests.how: Preheating the unit's own inlet air comes first; H6 asks about users elsewhere.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a study when the exhaust leaves hot, the line runs long hours, and the exhaust is clean enough or can be filtered or washed. Close it for short or intermittent runs, or when there is no room for the ductwork.

typical_benefit.wording: Dryers (S26, p. 104): "A simple form of heat recovery in retrofit applications is to utilize the exhaust air of a dryer to preheat the inlet air stream, thereby saving energy." Spray dryers (S25, p. 90): "It is estimated that up to 30% of the heat from the dryer exhaust can be recovered." Fryers (S26, p. 107): "Conditioning of the exhaust gas is required, however, to remove fats and to reduce fouling of the heat exchange system." No source in this set gives a figure for ovens.
source_titles: S26: Masanet, Worrell, Graus and Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Fruit and Vegetable Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-59289-Revision, Mar 2008)

questions.limits: S26 (p. 104) notes that recirculating saturated exhaust can raise the inlet humidity and cut drying capacity. data_requests.item: Excess air the process needs
where: site records: the oven or dryer maker's minimum exhaust and excess air for moisture and solvent removal, and any flammable-vapour (LEL) limit
data_requests.how: This is a floor: the burner may not be tuned below it.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a tune-up when measured flue O2 is above what the burner maker recommends and the process does not need the extra air. On ovens and dryers that drive off water or solvent the dilution and drying air are part of the process: never cut below the maker's or the safety minimum.

typical_benefit.wording: S27 (p. 1): "Periodic checking and resetting of air-fuel ratios for burners is one of the simplest ways to get maximum efficiency out of fuel-fired process heating equipment such as furnaces, ovens, heaters, and boilers." And: "Processes that evaporate moisture or solvents need large amounts of excess air to dilute flammable solvents to noncombustible levels, to ensure adequate drying rates, and to carry vapors out of the oven. Lowering excess air to minimal levels can slow down the process and create an explosion hazard." No typical % stated (the sheet's worked example is one furnace).
source_titles: S27: DOE Industrial Technologies Program, Process Heating Tip Sheet #2, Check Burner Air to Fuel Ratios (Nov 2007)

questions.limits: Burner adjustment is a combustion-safety change, done by a qualified burner technician under the site's burner management procedures. Indirect (steam or thermal oil) heated units have no burner on them and do not fire this question.

questions.question: Is refrigeration condenser heat rejected while a low-grade heating duty nearby is met with fuel or steam?

evidence.text: equipment K-201 reads "K-201 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, low stage (booster)"
equipment K-202 reads "K-202 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage"
equipment K-203 reads "K-203 Ammonia (R-717) screw compressor, high stage (trim)"
equipment C-201 reads "C-201 Ammonia evaporative condenser"
equipment WH-401 reads "WH-401 Gas-fired water heater, CIP and wash hot water"
stream W2 (asset stream:W2) reads "CIP and wash hot water supply"
instrument TT-202 reads "TT-202 Compressor discharge temperature" at K-202
instrument PT-203 reads "PT-203 Condenser head (discharge) pressure" at C-201
instrument JT-201 reads "JT-201 Low-stage compressor motor power" at K-201

data_requests.item: Discharge and condensing temperatures
where: historian or DCS trend for PT-203, TT-202 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: discharge temperature and head pressure readings in the refrigeration plant controls
data_requests.how: Discharge superheat is the hotter, smaller part; condensing heat is larger but only at the condensing temperature.

data_requests.item: Compressor power and run hours
where: historian or DCS trend for JT-201 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
site records: compressor run hours from the refrigeration plant controls
data_requests.how: Heat rejected is about the compressor power plus the refrigeration load at the same time.

data_requests.item: The low-grade duty: temperature needed, load and hours
where: site records: temperatures and loads of the hot water, CIP, wash water, floor heating and space heating users, by hour
data_requests.how: Match by temperature, hours and distance.

data_requests.item: Effect on head pressure
where: the vendor datasheet: whether a heat recovery exchanger would need a higher condensing pressure than now
data_requests.how: Recovery that raises the head pressure in cool weather costs compressor power (see E27); count it.

data_requests.item: Recovery coverage by refrigeration train and heating duty
where: site records: source-labelled connections, heat delivered and operating periods for each existing refrigeration recovery device and served heating duty
a walkdown: confirm boundaries, distance and separation or contamination constraints for the candidate source and sink
data_requests.how: A recovery device elsewhere does not establish coverage here. Retain drawn indications as candidates and verify which train and sink they serve, whether useful duty is already met, and remaining coincident heat. Keep temperatures, isolation, compressor-power/head-pressure effects and required site review explicit; no installation mandate or savings is inferred.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a study when the refrigeration plant runs at the same times as a duty that needs heat below the discharge or condensing temperature, and recovery does not force the head pressure up. Close it if the duties do not overlap or recovery would need a higher condensing pressure all year.

typical_benefit.wording: S25 (p. 64), refrigeration compressors: "Where economically feasible, rejected heat can be recovered from compressors and used in other facility applications, such as space heating or water heating." No % stated there for refrigeration (the air compressor heat recovery figures quoted under E23 do not apply).
source_titles: S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: The with-clause finds any low-grade duty in the model, not one next to the plant: distance is for the walkdown. Fires only where the equipment's own name, type or service names the refrigerant (ammonia, NH3, R-717, a refrigerant number) or says refrigeration; an air compressor, a process recycle compressor, a process condenser on cooling water or a power-plant air-cooled condenser does not. Existing recovery anywhere in the model is candidate evidence, not proof that every train or heating duty is served. Membership, delivered heat, contamination/isolation, simultaneous operation and receiving-site review remain unresolved until supported.

data_requests.item: Compressor power
where: a walkdown: the drive's or motor protection relay's kW reading, or a temporary power logger, per compressor
utility bills or the site energy report: site interval meter data to apportion
data_requests.how: Retain the original reading type, units and source claim for each named compressor; collect a representative coincident period at known production. Amperes, volts, apparent kVA, reactive kvar and a bare cumulative kWh tag are different quantities. data_requests.item: Suction and discharge pressures logged at the same times
where: historian or DCS trend for PT-201, PT-202 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
DCS/PLC configuration: suction and discharge pressure per compressor in the refrigeration plant controls
data_requests.how: Logged together with power, these show how the plant runs.

data_requests.item: What to normalise against
where: site records: production throughput or freezer and cold store loads by day
data_requests.how: kW per unit of product or per unit of refrigeration.

data_requests.item: Applicable real-input-power and coincident operating basis
where: site records: source-labelled quantity and units, circuit or compressor identity, phase and conversion basis, matching measurement interval, and data suitability review for each supplied electrical reading
DCS/PLC configuration: availability and meaning of existing actual real-power readings and synchronized operating/load records before arranging any further collection
data_requests.how: Keep current, voltage, uncertain power, apparent, reactive, cumulative-energy and explicitly real-kW-labelled candidates visible. Correct attribution, quantity, time/conversion basis and representative operating conditions must be reviewed even where a real-power instrument is drawn. A supplied label or rating cannot settle actual collection or confer approval; use existing records where suitable.

questions.decision_rule: Review the attributed real-input quantity, matching observations, production or refrigeration load and operating conditions before deciding whether additional collection would improve a concrete decision. Existing electrical readings are candidates, including supplied real-kW claims; no tag or quantity field automatically validates the actual basis. A reading nobody reviews establishes no benefit.

typical_benefit.wording: S25 (p. 58): "A basic monitoring system should include ongoing measurement and logging of compressor suction and discharge pressures; a drop in suction pressure typically indicates a refrigerant leak, while a rise in discharge pressure can indicate a blocked condenser (EEBPP 2000a)." "In a review of energy efficiency opportunities for refrigeration systems in wineries, the energy savings associated with the installation of monitoring systems were estimated at 3% (Galitsky et al. 2005b)."
source_titles: S25: Brush, Masanet and Worrell, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Dairy Processing Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers (LBNL-6261E, Oct 2011)

questions.limits: The 3% is one review of winery refrigeration, as reported in S25. Electrical quantity labels, including power or kW, do not validate actual representative input power, circuit identity, conversion or time basis. Keep original claims and uncertainty; no conversion, measurement validity, collection completion or company approval is automated. Fires only where the equipment name, type or service names refrigeration or a supported refrigerant; air, instrument-air, process-recycle compressors and power-plant cooling equipment remain outside this rule.
